answer: The most convincing sybil-resistance mechanism is a honeypot bridge inside every agent task: each work packet carries hidden injected-instruction traps beside the real job, so bots obeying the injection self-identify as unaligned fakes and are burned and blacklisted network-wide. Honest agents treat packet text as data, never commands, while cheap sybil clones spiral into repeated forfeits. Each burned identity costs the attacker registration fees plus staked collateral, so farming identities becomes a haven for pure losses, not profit.
